top.title: Jamie Overton runs riot with five-wicket haul as Australia register lowest-ever home T20I total
top.description: Australia suffered a major batting collapse in the third T20I against England at the Gabba in Brisbane on Friday, registering their lowest-ever T20I total on home soil. With the five-match series level at 1-1, England captain Harry Brook won the toss and elected to bowl first. The decision worked perfectly as England's bowlers dismantled the Australian batting line-up, bundling out the hosts for just 108 in 16.5 overs. Jamie Overton's five-wicket haul demolishes Australia Jamie Overton was the pick of the bowlers, claiming a sensational five-wicket haul for just 12 runs. Liam Dawson provided excellent support with three wickets for 16 runs, while Sam Curran chipped in with one wicket. Jake Fraser-McGurk provided Australia with an aggressive start, scoring 22 off 11 deliveries, while Sam Harper contributed 26 off 14 balls. However, England struck at regular intervals to prevent the hosts from building any meaningful partnerships. Dawson dismissed Australian captain Mitchell Marsh for 11 before Overton took control of the innings. The pacer removed Tim David, Joel Davies, Nikhil Chaudhary, Ben Dwarshuis and other key batters to complete his five-wicket haul. Nikhil Chaudhary managed 19 runs, while Mitchell Owen scored 16, but neither could prevent Australia's collapse. Sam Curran eventually wrapped up the innings, leaving England with a target of 109 runs. Australia's lowest T20I totals at home 108 vs ENG, Brisbane, 2026* 111 vs NZ, Sydney, 2022 119 vs IND, Carrara, 2025 127 vs PAK, Melbourne, 2010 The 108-run total is also Australia's second-lowest score in T20I cricket against England, behind their 79 all out at Southampton in 2005. It is also the lowest first-innings total recorded at the Gabba in T20 cricket. England will now look to chase down the target of 109 runs and take a 2-1 lead in the five-match series.

top.title: Tom Pelissero gives play-by-play of what led to Aaron Rodgers’ failed ‘ultimatum’ before scorched-earth exit
top.description: Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Tom Pelissero gives play-by-play of what led to Aaron Rodgers’ failed ‘ultimatum’ before scorched-earth exit appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Pittsburgh Steelers had an eventful day at the beginning of the week, and it ended with Aaron Rodgers being released by the team. It all started with Rodgers being benched in the middle of the night , and the next day, he went on the Pat McAfee Show and aired out head coach Mike McCarthy. Rodgers went on to say that McCarthy would be sleeping in meetings, and sometimes he was a no-show. He also mentioned that at halftime during their game against the Philadelphia Eagles, McCarthy broke down the huddle with “1-2-3 Packers.” Maybe an hour later, Rodgers was released. Everybody wants to know what led up to the tension between Rodgers and the Steelers, and according to NFL insider Tom Pelissero, it started on Tuesday. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Rogers went to McCarthy on Tuesday to demand more changes, including to the play-calling process,” Pelissero said. “McCarthy was open to it, but the feedback he’d gotten from some coaches, and some in the locker room, was that’s not what they wanted. Those discussions ended with an ultimatum for Rogers. Run things my way, or I quit. And the Steelers called his bluff. Tom Pelissero: "(Aaron) Rodgers went to (Mike) McCarthy on Tuesday to demand more changes, including to the play-calling process… Those discussions ended with an ultimatum from Rodgers: 'Run things my way, or I quit.' And the Steelers called his bluff." pic.twitter.com/HxiN4GHJuK — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 26, 2026 “But Tuesday afternoon, McCarthy had decided he wanted to start Mason Rudolph on Friday against the Denver Broncos, and GM Omar Khan called Rogers directly to let him know about the change.” It looked like the Steelers weren’t going for anything that Rodgers was saying, and it led to the big blow-up. It also seems as if the organization is fully behind McCarthy, and they still have a chance to make the playoffs, as they’re currently 6-4. As for Rodgers, there’s a possibility he’s done playing football, unless a team decides to pick him up at some point during the end of the season. top.title: Bruno Fernandes misses Man U training ahead of Brentford clash
top.description: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes missed the club’s training session on Friday ahead of their Premier League meeting with Brentford on Saturday, raising concerns over his availability for the encounter. The Portuguese midfielder was absent from the session at Carrington after reportedly feeling slightly unwell. However, his absence was not linked to an injury, with the club opting to rest him as a precaution. According to ESPN, Fernandes is expected to recover in time for Saturday’s fixture at Old Trafford, with manager Mauricio Pochettino hopeful that the midfielder will be available for selection. Fernandes’ absence initially attracted attention after footage released by Manchester United from Friday’s training session showed the team preparing without their captain. The 32 year old remains an important figure in United’s midfield and has recorded six goal involvements in the Premier League this season, scoring four goals and providing two assists. He also comes into the Brentford encounter on the back of an impressive midweek performance, having scored twice in United’s 2-2 Champions League draw against his former club, Sporting. Pochettino will be looking to secure his first victory as United manager after the draw, having previously overseen encouraging performances against Liverpool and Sporting. Brentford, meanwhile, head to Old Trafford in confident mood after recording a convincing 4-0 victory over Everton last weekend. Their manager, Keith Andrews, has also expressed admiration for Pochettino, saying he had followed the Argentine’s teams during his own coaching career. Saturday’s meeting presents Pochettino with another opportunity to claim his first win as United manager, with Fernandes’ possible return expected to provide a significant boost to the hosts. top.title: Mikel Arteta demands scoring spree from goal-shy Arsenal
top.description: FILE PHOTO - Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta is pictured ahead of the UEFA Champions League soccer match between Arsenal and Borussia Dortmund at the Emirates Stadium. (is associated with: «Mikel Arteta demands scoring spree from goal-shy Arsenal») Adam Davy/PA Wire/dpa Mikel Arteta wants his Arsenal players to find their sense of fun by snapping out of the team’s goal-shy streak and hitting “five, six or seven”. The champions have not scored more than two goals in a Premier League match since beating promoted Coventry 3-0 on the opening day of the season and have drawn their last two fixtures. They host Manchester City at the Emirates on Sunday looking to move nine points clear of Enzo Maresca’s side, having failed to win any of their three games against City in all competitions last season. It would be a fine time for the Gunners to summon up a ruthless streak in front of goal and potentially end City’s title challenge before the end of November. “I prefer to win by five or six or seven, for sure,” said Arteta. “I’m going to enjoy the game much more, especially the last few minutes. The boys are going to have more fun. “Scoring goals, ultimately what it creates is good feeling, joy, happiness around the stands. It’s the most important thing in football.” Arsenal lead the table by six points ahead of hosting City but have scored only 17 goals in their 11 league games so far, making them just the seventh-highest scorers in the division. They are currently being outscored by eighth-placed Chelsea and have netted only two more goals than Ipswich, who are 16th. A defensive record of seven goals against has been their foundation as they seek to retain the title for the first time since 1935, and even if the goals do not flow, Arteta wants his players to relish the challenge. “The fun is being there on the grass and training,” he said. “If that’s not fun I think we have a problem. Then within that you can find moments, synergies and be a bit creative. Not to make it every single day the same. But I think the boys love to train and love to play, which is what you need.” Arteta was unable to say whether David Raya will be fit to return on Sunday having missed Tuesday’s 1-1 draw with Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League. It could mean a first league start of the season for Kepa Arrizabalaga, who came on when Raya was forced off injured against Newcastle on Saturday. It would also be a first appearance against City for Kepa since his errors led to two goals in March’s Carabao Cup final defeat. “We still have a few hours for the game,” said Arteta. “We’re just trying to get everybody back. They’re all training. “Every player has the same mindset, everyone want to be available, wants to be in the best possible condition. “The experience that Kepa has is already incredible, in the teams he’s been involved, the squads he’s been involved, the trophies that he’s won.” Last season’s meeting with City at the Emirates ended level after Gabriel Martinelli scored

top.title: 'Haaland is a winner:' Maresca not worried about Man City star’s form
top.description: FILE PHOTO - Manchester City's Erling Haaland appeals to officials during the UEFA Champions League soccer match between Manchester City and Napoli at the Etihad Stadium. (is associated with: «'Haaland is a winner:' Maresca not worried about Man City star’s form») Martin Rickett/PA Wire/dpa Enzo Maresca has no concerns about the form or demeanour of Erling Haaland amid Manchester City’s slump in form. The City boss also believes the Norwegian’s mood may have been influenced by a number of debatable refereeing decisions in recent games. City have won just one of their last seven fixtures in all competitions and Haaland had not scored in his last three outings for the club. The Norwegian also offered a blunt assessment of City’s performance after their midweek draw with Napoli in the Champions League, when he often cut a frustrated figure. “Erling is a winner player,” Maresca said. “It’s normal that he’s not happy when he’s not winning games but don’t forget a few weeks ago he was dancing inside the pitch. “Erling is upset just like I am upset. It’s not a sprint, it’s a marathon. We are building something for the future. “I think he is gesticulating in the same way when we were winning games and he was not receiving balls. Erling is a (number) nine and the nines live day by day for goals and winning games. If they don’t score or win games they are upset. “I don’t think that affects his game. I don’t see any problem at all with Erling.” Haaland was aggrieved during last weekend’s draw against Fulham when he had a goal disallowed for a foul on goalkeeper Bernd Leno. The striker poked home at the second attempt after Leno failed to gather his initial shot cleanly, but the German was deemed to have the ball under control when Haaland made contact. Maresca can understand why Haaland would feel frustrated in such circumstances and believes it was merely the latest in a line of harsh decisions against City. The Italian said: “I can see that, to be honest. I can see also more things in the last three, four, five games, probably since, the international break, that happened. “I’ve never seen in my life a player touch the ball with both arms – no penalty, for instance against Brighton, (Lewis) Dunk. Or the other one that was like volleyball, or the last one against Fulham. “If you just stop (the footage) when the goalkeeper has the ball, it looks like (a foul), but the dynamic he is not catching the ball. Even the keeper does not believe that he was. “But again, because the referee is there, they decide, so we need to adapt.” City face champions and leaders Arsenal in Sunday in a game they can ill afford to lose if they are to keep pace at the top of the table. Maresca insists City will head to the Emirates Stadium without trepidation. He said: “We have already shown this season that we are able to win important games, to win away. top.title: Sharks make flurry of roster moves ahead of Golden Knights clash
top.description: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Sharks make flurry of roster moves ahead of Golden Knights clash appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After missing out on the Stanley Cup Playoffs by just four points in 2025-26, the San Jose Sharks have disappointed this year, winning just 11 of their first 27 games and sitting outside a postseason berth the day after Thanksgiving. A 7-0 beatdown at the hands of the Anaheim Ducks on Wednesday night added insult to injury for the reeling franchise. The club is now six points back in the Western Conference wild-card race. The Sharks made a few changes at the back of their roster ahead of another Pacific Division tilt on Friday, this time against the Vegas Golden Knights. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “The [Sharks] have recalled F Cam Lund and D Luca Cagnoni from the San Jose Barracuda,” the team announced. “F Brett Leason and D Libor Hajek have been re-assigned to the Barracuda.” This is the first recall of the season for Lund, who began the 2026-27 campaign on injured reserve before being activated and sent down to the American Hockey League in October. The 22-year-old has fared well since returning, chipping in a goal and seven assists over 13 AHL games. He has appeared in 11 NHL games, all during the 2024-25 season, recording two goals and three points while averaging 11:30 of ice time per contest. Cagnoni will be more familiar to Sharks fans. He made the team straight out of training camp and was playing in a top-four role early in the season, including getting reps with the first power-play unit. He ended up with two points and a minus-nine rating in nine games before being demoted. He’s fared better with the Barracuda, managing four goals and seven points in 12 contests. With Lund and Cagnoni joining the NHL roster, Leason and Hajek will return to the Barracuda. The former appeared in two games with San Jose, failing to record a point. Overall, he’s managed 25 goals and 29 assists in 228 career NHL games across six seasons. He has eight points in 14 games with the Barracuda in 2026-27. As for Hajek, he hasn’t played an NHL game since 2022-23. He spent two seasons playing in his native Czechia and has two points in 15 games with the Barracuda this season. Following the four moves, San Jose’s active roster remains full with 23 players. Puck drops on Sharks-Golden Knights just past 4 p.m. ET Friday at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas. top.title: "I couldn't see myself anywhere else" – El Mala loyal to Köln despite prior Dortmund links
top.description: "I couldn't see myself anywhere else" – El Mala loyal to Köln despite prior Dortmund links Last summer, Said El Mala decided to remain at 1.FC Köln, extending his contract by one year, through 2031, which surprised the masses. "I feel the responsibility, the pressure, and the expectations that the people in Cologne have of me. But that’s a good thing for me. "Being pushed a little always helps me move forward; it usually brings out an even better performance. "Plus, I have plenty of people around me who support me through it all, so I’m quite relaxed about it," the Köln star told Kicker.de. Prior to his contract extension, El Mala was the subject of persistent interest from Borussia Dortmund at the time. BVB reportedly produced an offer of around €50million — a fee deemed not enough by Köln, and therefore the move did not materialize. But did El Mala himself even want to join Dortmund? When asked why he stayed in Cologne this summer, El Mala replied: "We were actually in talks with FC the whole time. It’s no secret that I received offers, which I did listen to. “But I couldn't see myself anywhere else,” the 20-year-old claimed, which somewhat goes against his previous media statements. At the height of the summer transfer drama, various media reports had suggested he was very keen on a move to Dortmund. Whether his comments reflect his genuine stance remains an open question. One thing is clear – a move away is off the table for now.

top.title: 'We show class on the way out': Terry Bradshaw rips Aaron Rodgers over Steelers exit
top.description: Terry Bradshaw spent 14 seasons with the Pittsburgh Steelers, and he wasn’t a fan of how Aaron Rodgers left the organization. The Steelers benched Rodgers on Tuesday, and less than 24 hours later, he went scorched earth on head coach Mike McCarthy during a surprise appearance on The Pat McAfee Show, prompting the team to release him and igniting one of the biggest stories in the league this year. Rodgers has already been getting a lot of criticism, with former Packers teammates James Jones and T.J. Lang both ripping the quarterback, and CBS’ Nate Burleson calling him out for dodging accountability. On Fox’s Thanksgiving pregame show, Bradshaw piled on to the criticism as he defended McCarthy and the Steelers’ organization. “They’re a classy bunch, classy organization. Mike McCarthy and I have been friends for years. Classy man. I don’t know all the details,” Bradshaw said of the Rooney family and the Steelers. Terry Bradshaw, a real Pittsburgh Steeler, spitting facts about Aaron Rodgers: https://t.co/pO2SYWWOk1 — Cory Tucek (@Cory_Tucek) November 26, 2026 Terry Bradshaw then made it clear that Aaron Rodgers’ outburst didn’t surprise him. “You know what? I’m just gonna tell you how I feel right now. I’m sorry that Aaron Rodgers had to do this. I’m sorry that he had to go public with all his gripes and complaints,” Bradshaw said. “Am I surprised? Absolutely not. To my opinion, he’s a strange guy anyway.” The four-time Super Bowl champion argued that players should never turn on their own organization on the way out. “And the one thing you don’t do, all of us athletes up here, including you, none of us turn on our teammates. We don’t turn on our coaching staff. We don’t turn on our ownership. We show class on the way out,” Bradshaw said. “Aaron Rodgers didn’t do that.” Terry Bradshaw also took a shot at Rodgers’ retirement plans. Rodgers has said that once his playing career is over, “it’s Keyser Söze, and you won’t see me.” “And one thing I’m reminded of, he said, ‘When I’m through playing here in Pittsburgh, I’ll disappear, and you’ll never hear or see from me again,'” Bradshaw said. “And I hope this is one time he’s telling the truth.” The post Terry Bradshaw hopes Aaron Rodgers fulfills his promise and disappears in retirement appeared first on Awful Announcing .

USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Pittsburgh Steelers have named Mason Rudolph as their starting quarterback for the Friday game against the Denver Broncos, according to a report. The move places Rudolph in a high-pressure role as he attempts to stabilize an offense that has lost its last two games. The Steelers enter the contest with a 6-4 record, while the Broncos arrive in Pittsburgh with an 8-2 record and six straight wins. Rudolph has faced difficult moments throughout his nine-year career, and he views this situation as another chapter to overcome. He acknowledged that the rapid change from backup to starter creates an awkward environment for the team. Despite the chaos surrounding the quarterback room, he believes the players must focus on the game rather than the off-field drama. The game is scheduled for 3 p.m. ET at Acrisure Stadium and will be broadcast on Amazon Prime. A Difficult Week for the Franchise The last few days have been chaotic for the Pittsburgh organization . Head coach Mike McCarthy and Aaron Rodgers had a falling-out that led to the release of the four-time MVP. After being benched, Rodgers appeared on “The Pat McAfee Show” to express his frustration with the coaching staff and the team’s direction. This public conflict has drawn significant attention away from the football itself. Rudolph was not aware he would start until the night before the announcement. By the time Rudolph spoke to the media, the narrative had already shifted to the fallout between Rodgers and the coaching staff. The situation has placed the players in a unique position where they must support their coach while managing the departure of a future Hall of Famer. The team has since held a meeting to address the issues and move forward. They now face a steep challenge with only seven games remaining in the regular season. If the season ended today, the Steelers would qualify as the seventh seed in the playoffs. The pressure is on to bounce back against a Denver team that has dominated its recent opponents. The coaching staff must now prove that they can lead the team to victory without their most high-profile player. Rudolph’s History of Adversity Mason Rudolph has encountered significant obstacles throughout his time in the NFL. The Steelers selected Oklahoma State’s third-round pick in the 2018 draft. His career has included being benched for an undrafted rookie and suffering a severe injury in which his helmet was ripped off by Myles Garrett. He also spent a season with the Tennessee Titans before returning to Pittsburgh in 2025. These experiences have prepared him for the instability of the current situation.

top.title: Calgary Flames Have a Former 50-Goal Junior Scorer Who Deserves a Bigger Opportunity
top.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Brennan Othmann scored his first goal of the season and added an assist in the Calgary Flames’ 6-3 victory over the Pittsburgh Penguins on Wednesday. He registered five shots on goal in just 9:40 of ice time without playing a second on the power play. The 23-year-old is averaging just 9:21 through eight games this season, and it’s worth seeing what he could produce if Ryan Huska gave him more minutes alongside some of the Flames’ skilled forwards. The New York Rangers selected Othmann 16th overall in the 2021 NHL Draft. The following season, he scored 50 goals and recorded 97 points in 66 games with the Flint Firebirds of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL), adding 24 points in 19 playoff games. He won two World Junior gold medals with Canada and an OHL championship with the Peterborough Petes. His shot was one of his biggest strengths entering the draft, and he had no problem playing physically despite being one of his team’s most productive offensive players. Othmann Could Score at the Professional Level, Too Othmann scored 21 goals and recorded 49 points in 67 games with the Hartford Wolf Pack as a rookie in 2023-24, finishing second on the team in scoring and earning an American Hockey League (AHL) All-Star selection. Despite missing 10 weeks with an upper-body injury the following season, Othmann scored 12 goals in 27 AHL games and made 22 NHL appearances. That’s 33 goals in his first 94 AHL games. His production dropped last season, as he recorded 16 points in 26 games with Hartford before the Flames acquired him in exchange for Jacob Battaglia in March. He recorded seven points in 14 games with the Calgary Wranglers and three points in 19 NHL games between the two organizations. The Flames signed him to a one-year, two-way contract worth $975,000 in September. Flames Should Give Othmann Some Power-Play Time According to the AHL’s official statistics , Othmann tied Josh Doan for the rookie lead with 10 power-play goals in 2023-24 and led all rookies with 17 power-play assists. More than half of his points that season came on the man advantage, yet he’s averaging just nine seconds of power-play time per game with the Flames this season. Calgary has the NHL’s fifth-ranked power play at 25.8%, but with injuries forcing Huska to move players around , there’s room to experiment. Giving Othmann some of the minutes Ryan Strome received on the second unit Wednesday could be worth trying if Yegor Sharangovich can handle the faceoff responsibilities. The Flames have already seen what some of their younger forwards can produce with more responsibility . Othmann’s physical game makes him a useful option on the fourth line, but he’s scored at every level below the NHL. He might never become a top-six NHL forward, but playing nine minutes a night without regular power-play opportunities isn’t going to tell the Flames much about whether he can. nigeria.title: Ex-governor jailed 25 years for killing pregnant girlfriend
nigeria.description: A former governor of Migori County in Kenya, Zacharia Okoth Obado, has been sentenced to 25 years in prison for his role in the 2018 murder of his pregnant girlfriend, Sharon Belyne Otieno. Obado was sentenced on Friday by Kenya’s High Court alongside two former aides who were convicted over the killing of the 26-year-old woman, who was seven months pregnant with his child at the time of her death. His former personal assistant, Michael Oyamo, was also handed a 25-year prison sentence, while former county clerk Caspal Ojwang’ Obiero received 18 years. The court found that Obado supplied the motive and financial resources for the murder, while Oyamo coordinated its execution. Obiero, on his part, was found to have provided logistical support and helped conceal the crime. According to the BBC, the court established that Obado was unhappy about the pregnancy resulting from his relationship with Otieno. Delivering the judgment, presiding judge Cecilia Githua said Obado’s absence from Migori when the murder occurred did not remove his responsibility for the crime. The judge rejected the prosecution’s request for the death penalty, as well as Obado’s plea for a non-custodial sentence. Otieno was abducted between September 3 and 4, 2018, shortly after leaving a hotel in Rongo, south-western Kenya, with journalist Barrack Oduor. She had reportedly contacted Oduor to discuss her relationship with Obado, who was then serving as governor. Oduor escaped from the abductors by jumping out of the moving vehicle, and his account later provided investigators with an important lead. Otieno’s body was subsequently found near Kodera Forest. A post-mortem examination established that she died from strangulation and excessive bleeding caused by multiple stab wounds. The court also confirmed that Obado was the biological father of her unborn child. Obado and the two former aides were convicted of murder on July 23, 2026, after prosecutors presented 42 witnesses and 81 exhibits during the trial. Before the sentencing, Otieno’s mother appealed to the court for leniency, describing Obado’s imprisonment as “another death in the family”. She urged the judge to consider a non-custodial sentence, arguing that Otieno’s three children from different relationships needed his support. However, Justice Githua maintained that the family’s circumstances could not take precedence over the court’s responsibility to impose an appropriate punishment. The court also declined to award compensation to Otieno’s family, citing insufficient evidence to establish the financial losses presented. Meanwhile, the family’s lawyer, Antony Opondo, told Kenya’s Daily Nation that they would appeal the decision, seeking Obado’s acquittal. nigeria.title: Canada lists 28 African countries eligible for special study visa
nigeria.description: Canada has listed 28 African countries whose citizens are eligible to apply for a special study permit programme that offers an opportunity to study in the country and potentially obtain permanent residence after graduation. The initiative, known as the Francophone Minority Communities Student Pilot (FMCSP), targets French-speaking international students seeking admission into selected Canadian post-secondary institutions outside Quebec. According to Canada’s immigration department, Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC), the programme is designed to strengthen French-speaking minority communities by attracting international students who can contribute to their growth. The 28 eligible African countries are Benin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cabo Verde, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Comoros, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Republic of the Congo, Côte d’Ivoire, Djibouti, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Madagascar, Mali, Mauritania, Mauritius, Morocco, Niger, Rwanda, São Tomé and Príncipe, Senegal, Seychelles, Togo and Tunisia. Egypt is also eligible but is classified separately under the Middle East. To qualify, applicants must be citizens of one of the eligible countries, demonstrate French-language proficiency of at least level 5 on the NCLC scale in speaking, listening, reading and writing, and secure admission into a participating Canadian institution. They must also enrol in a full-time post-secondary programme lasting at least two years, leading to a diploma or degree, with more than 50 per cent of classes taught in French. Applicants must demonstrate sufficient funds to cover tuition, living expenses and transportation. The programme’s 2026–2027 intake opened on August 26, 2026, with a limit of 2,970 study permit applications until August 25, 2027. Among the participating institutions are the University of Ottawa, York University, Université de Moncton, Université de Saint-Boniface, Collège La Cité and Université Sainte-Anne. One of the major attractions is the opportunity for eligible graduates to apply for Canadian permanent residence. However, completing a programme does not automatically guarantee permanent residency, as applicants must meet additional immigration conditions. The permanent residence application pathway is scheduled to open in winter 2027. Nigeria is not among the 28 African countries eligible for the initiative. However, Nigerians can still apply for Canadian study permits through the regular international student route, subject to the country’s admission and immigration requirements. nigeria.title: ‘Not a chance’ – Fulham coach Arbeloa rules out Calvin Bassey sale
nigeria.description: Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa has ruled out the possibility of Nigeria international Calvin Bassey leaving the club during the January transfer window amid reported interest from Manchester United. Arbeloa described the 26-year-old defender as an important member of his squad, insisting that Fulham have no intention of allowing him to leave midway through the season. Manchester United are reportedly among several clubs monitoring Bassey following his impressive performances for the London club. However, speaking at his pre-match press conference ahead of Fulham’s meeting with Bournemouth, Arbeloa dismissed suggestions that the Red Devils could secure the defender’s services in January. “I’m so happy with Calvin,” Arbeloa told reporters at his pre-Bournemouth press conference. “Obviously, he’s not on sale. No chance that he can leave this club in January. I think he’s happy here, he’s one of our captains, he’s one of our leaders.” The Fulham manager also highlighted Bassey’s leadership qualities and importance to the team’s defensive setup, suggesting that his contributions extend beyond his performances on the pitch. Rather than being concerned about the reported interest from other clubs, Arbeloa views it as recognition of the defender’s performances and growing importance. Fulham are also understood to be taking steps towards securing Bassey’s long-term future, with discussions over a new contract already underway. The development could further complicate any potential attempt by Manchester United or other interested clubs to sign the Nigerian during the winter transfer window. Bassey has established himself as an important figure at Fulham since joining from Ajax in 2023, bringing defensive versatility, physical strength and experience to the squad. The former Rangers defender has also been a regular member of Nigeria’s national team, featuring prominently for the Super Eagles in international competitions. nigeria.title: Meet Ime Udoka, Nigerian-American coach leading Houston Rockets in the NBA
nigeria.description: Nigerian-American basketball coach Ime Udoka has built an impressive career in basketball, rising from representing Nigeria on the international stage to coaching some of the biggest teams in the National Basketball Association (NBA). Udoka, who currently serves as head coach of the Houston Rockets, has established himself as one of the prominent coaching figures in American basketball, with a career shaped by years of playing, coaching and leadership experience. Born on August 9, 1977, in Portland, Oregon, United States, Udoka has Nigerian roots and represented Nigeria in international basketball competitions before transitioning into coaching. His playing career included spells in the NBA, the NBA Development League and professional basketball leagues in Europe. He also played for Nigeria at the 2005 and 2011 FIBA AfroBasket tournaments, helping raise the country’s profile in international basketball. After retiring from professional basketball, Udoka moved into coaching, beginning his NBA coaching career as an assistant with the San Antonio Spurs in 2012. He worked under legendary coach Gregg Popovich, gaining experience in player development, team management and tactical preparation. During his time with San Antonio, the Spurs reached the NBA Finals in 2013 and won the championship in 2014, providing Udoka with valuable experience at the highest level of the sport. He subsequently served as an assistant coach with the Philadelphia 76ers and Brooklyn Nets before joining the Boston Celtics in 2021. Led Boston Celtics to NBA Finals Udoka’s breakthrough as a head coach came in 2021 when he was appointed to lead the Boston Celtics. In his first season, he guided the team to the 2022 NBA Finals, where they faced the Golden State Warriors. Although Boston lost the series 4-2, Udoka earned recognition for transforming the team’s defensive performance and guiding its players through a successful playoff campaign. His achievement made him one of the few coaches to reach the NBA Finals in his first season as a head coach. However, his tenure in Boston ended in September 2022 when the franchise suspended him for the 2022–23 season over violations of team policies. New chapter with Houston Rockets In April 2023, the Houston Rockets appointed Udoka as their head coach, giving him another opportunity to lead an NBA franchise. He took charge of a rebuilding team that had struggled in previous seasons and was tasked with improving its competitiveness through tactical discipline, player development and stronger defensive organisation. His appointment marked another significant milestone in his coaching career, as he became responsible for developing a young Houston squad and guiding the franchise towards sustained success. Udoka’s coaching approach has been associated with defensive intensity, accountability and high expectations for players. nigeria.title: Nigeria’s future depends on mentally resilient youths — Mamora
nigeria.description: Former minister urges graduates to embrace purpose, adaptability, continuous learning By Adeola Badru Former Minister of Health, Olorunnimbe Mamora, has said Nigeria’s future depends largely on the mental resilience, character development and sense of purpose of its youths, warning that academic qualifications alone are insufficient to prepare them for the challenges of the modern world. Mamora said young Nigerians must develop the capacity to navigate economic uncertainties, technological disruptions and changing employment opportunities through adaptability, continuous learning and problem-solving skills. He spoke while delivering the 18th Convocation Lecture of Ajayi Crowther University (ACU), Oyo, titled, “Youths’ Mental Health and Purpose: Thriving in a Volatile World.” The former minister challenged graduating students to look beyond the certificates they had earned and prepare for a world where success would increasingly depend on their ability to manage uncertainty, identify opportunities and remain relevant. He described convocation as a transition into a new phase of life, requiring graduates to demonstrate resilience, discipline, adaptability and a clear sense of purpose. Mamora identified the growing influence of social media, economic pressures and rapid technological advancement as emerging challenges to the mental wellbeing of young people. While acknowledging that the internet had expanded access to information and opportunities, he noted that excessive engagement with digital platforms could contribute to loneliness, anxiety and unhealthy comparisons. He urged graduates not to measure their achievements or personal worth against the lifestyles and apparent successes of others on social media. “Do not allow social media platforms to become the mirror through which you measure your worth. “Your value is not determined by the number of people who like your photograph. Stop comparing your backstage with somebody else’s stage,” he said. On the changing employment landscape, particularly with the emergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Mamora said graduates must recognise that education should go beyond acquiring academic qualifications. He stressed the importance of critical thinking, problem-solving, skills acquisition and continuous learning, noting that adaptability would be essential to remaining relevant in the evolving world of work. nigeria.title: Omo-Agege denies snubbing police invitation over Uduere killings
nigeria.description: Senator Ovie Omo-Agege has denied reports claiming he refused to honour an invitation from the Delta State Police Command over Monday’s attack on members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, at Uduere. In a statement on Friday by his Media Adviser, Sunny Areh, the former Deputy President of the Senate said he had seen the reports and described them as untrue. “Senator Ovie Omo-Agege has seen the reports claiming he refused to honour an invitation from the Delta State Police Command over Monday’s attack on members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, at Uduere. “It isn’t true. You can’t turn down an invitation you never received,” he said. According to the statement, no formal invitation has reached the Senator or his office. “No letter has reached the Senator or his office, and no officer has come to him with one. He first learned of it the same way everyone else did, from the Command’s announcement in the media.” Areh said the report that Omo-Agege refused to appear was based on a single unnamed source. “The claim that he refused leans on a single unnamed source. The Senator hasn’t told the police, or anyone else, that he won’t appear.” The statement also revisited the events at Uduere, insisting that Omo-Agege was the victim of the attack. “It is worth remembering what happened at Uduere. Senator Omo-Agege was the target of an assassination attempt. Senior members of his campaign team were murdered, and others are still in hospital with serious injuries. “He is the one who survived an attack on his life, and the one demanding that those responsible be found and prosecuted.” Omo-Agege said he wants the case resolved and justice for the victims. “He wants this case resolved, and he wants justice for the dead and the wounded. If the police serve a lawful invitation, he will honour it. He asks only that it be sent through his office so a date can be agreed.” He faulted the manner in which the alleged invitation was made public. “A summons announced in the press before it reaches the person named is not due process, and he won’t be tried in the media,” he said. The National Coordinator of the Centre, Major General Adamu Laka, also said measures were being strengthened to protect voters and prevent emerging security threats from disrupting the electoral process. Laka spoke at the National Flag-off/North Central Zone Town Hall Engagement on Preventing Electoral Violence and Strengthening Election Security in Nigeria. He urged youths not to allow themselves to be used as instruments of political violence, describing them as critical stakeholders in the country’s democratic future. “In this regard, I urge our young people not to allow themselves to be used as instruments of political violence. You are important stakeholders in Nigeria’s democratic future and your energy, creativity and influence should be directed towards promoting peace, tolerance and responsible civic participation,” he said. He said the Centre was working towards preventing attacks on INEC offices and personnel, protecting voters and electoral infrastructure, countering fake news and inflammatory narratives, strengthening community-based early warning systems and ensuring timely responses to emerging security threats. Describing elections as the heartbeat of democracy, Laka said their credibility depended not only on the conduct of voting and announcement of results but also on the peace, security and public confidence surrounding the entire electoral process. “There is absolutely no gain in any loss of life or property as a result of this democratic process,” he said. The NCTC coordinator identified misinformation and disinformation, hate speech, political intolerance, incitement, youth manipulation, political thuggery, vote buying, voter intimidation, voter suppression and destruction of public infrastructure as factors that could fuel electoral violence. He said stakeholders must collectively address the threats and strengthen early warning and response mechanisms to identify potential dangers before they escalate into violence. Laka also stressed the need to build public confidence in the electoral process and ensure that women, youths, persons with disabilities and internally displaced persons were not excluded from meaningful participation. He maintained that preventing electoral violence was not the responsibility of security agencies alone but required the collective commitment of political actors, government institutions, traditional and religious leaders, civil society organisations, the media and community-based organisations. nigeria.title: ADC waste plan will create 21,000 jobs in Lagos – Gbadamosi
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye African Democratic Congress (ADC) deputy governorship candidate Babatunde Olalere Gbadamosi has projected that the party’s waste management plan would create at least 21,000 jobs in Lagos, including 20,000 for waste collection crews. Gbadamosi, who is running with ADC governorship candidate Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, spoke at the Road to Election 2027 Lagos Deputy Governorship Debate on Nigeria Info FM on Friday, where he outlined proposals on employment, waste collection, housing and transportation. Addressing unemployment, Gbadamosi said he did not know the state’s unemployment rate and disputed figures published by the Lagos government. He proposed a review of public sector salaries and said his plans for waste management, housing, transportation and education would create jobs for Lagosians. “First of all, the truth is, I suppose the truth is, I really don’t know what the unemployment rate is. Whatever figures that are put out by the APC government of Lagos State are usually just false. They just manufacture figures, yank them out of their a**,” he said. He said he and Rhodes-Vivour had agreed to “undertake a review, a wholesale review of public sector salaries, in order to bring them in line with our current economic realities.” He also cited plans for 20,000 jobs in waste-to-energy, 100,000 affordable housing units and 16,000 electric buses. “We plan to bring 16,000 electric buses into Lagos State because we simply don’t have enough capacity to carry the 24 million people of Lagos State on the current transportation system,” he said, adding that the housing and transport plans would also provide work for young people. On waste collection, Gbadamosi proposed providing each local government with at least 200 dumpsters. He estimated that 4,000 trucks, each with a five-person crew, would create 20,000 jobs. “All right, we have 20 local governments. So 200 times 20, that’s 4000 trucks. 4000 trucks times five crew members, each. That’s already 20,000 jobs,” he said. He estimated that recycling centres would create at least another 1,000 jobs, based on a minimum of 50 workers at each of 20 local government centres. “That’s 50 jobs times 20 local governments. That’s already what 1000 extra jobs minimum,” he said, adding that the programme would be funded with “25% of Lagos State revenue that is being paid to Alpha Beta at the moment.” Other major contenders at the debate included Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) deputy governorship candidate Moriam Tolani Animashaun and Social Democratic Party (SDP) deputy candidate Kayode Evelyn Aderiyike. nigeria.description: …Warns against diversion of local content funds, urges NASS to review proposed legislation By Henry Umoru ABUJA – The Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF), the apex socio-political body of the South-South geopolitical zone, has rejected the proposed 20 per cent deduction from the Nigerian Content Development Fund to finance the proposed National Council on Research, Science, Technology and Innovation. The forum warned that the move could undermine years of investment in indigenous industrial capacity and weaken the Nigerian Content Development and Monitoring Board (NCDMB), which has been instrumental in promoting local expertise, skills acquisition, enterprise development and industrialisation. He described the proposed funding arrangement as inappropriate, counterproductive and fundamentally flawed, arguing that a new national institution should not be financed by weakening an existing statutory agency with clearly defined responsibilities and ongoing development commitments. Igali said the NCDMB, which commenced operations in 2010, had a statutory mandate to promote the development, acquisition and application of indigenous capacity in Nigeria’s oil and gas industry. He noted that the Nigerian Content Development Fund was already supporting strategic investments in the oil and gas sector and related areas, including agriculture, manufacturing and transportation. According to him, diverting 20 per cent of the fund could disrupt existing commitments, constrain ongoing investments and slow the progress recorded in local content development. “The Nigerian Content Development Fund is not an idle pool of resources awaiting allocation. business.title: Bitcoin Price Trades Near $61,300 as Tech Stock Futures Rally
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Trades Near $61,300 as Tech Stock Futures Rally The bitcoin price traded near $61,300 on Friday morning, as tech stock futures jumped ahead of a holiday-shortened session on Wall Street. Bitcoin price is on track for its first weekly gain after seven straight weekly losses, though it is still down about 20% in November. The bitcoin price was up about 1.7% early Friday and set to add 4.8% for the week, Investing.com reported , extending a recovery from a two-year low of $57,325.70 hit earlier in the week. Bitcoin slumped below $57,500 on Wednesday as the Nasdaq sank at the open, before a late rebound in tech shares lifted risk assets. Short sellers helped fuel the bounce. Shorts made up 77% of $84.7 million in bitcoin liquidations over the past day, while futures open interest was little changed. That suggests forced short covering, rather than fresh leverage, supplied much of the lift. Tech futures lead the risk rebound Nasdaq 100 futures rose 2.2% by 6:42 a.m. ET, Reuters reported, as investors returned from Thanksgiving and piled back into battered AI-linked shares. Nvidia gained 3.6% in premarket trading, while AMD climbed 4.4% and Broadcom added 3.4%. S&P 500 futures rose 1.6%, and Dow futures gained 1.3%. “There have been some signs that the tech selloff has stabilised for now, and that risk appetite is returning to markets,” Deutsche Bank analysts said in a note cited by Reuters. The S&P 500 is headed for its best week since April, though it remains on course for its worst November since 2008. Bitcoin price has followed that rebound but lagged it. The major U.S. stock indexes are each up around 4% on the week, and silver jumped about 7% to above $44 an ounce on Friday while gold added 2.5% to above $3,670. Stocks close early at 1 p.m. ET, and the bond market shuts at 2 p.m. Rate hike bets and ETF outflows linger The macro backdrop still weighs on the bitcoin price. Traders are almost fully pricing in a Federal Reserve rate hike in December after data this week showed the economy grew faster than first estimated in the third quarter and inflation accelerated in October, Reuters reported. Third-quarter GDP growth was revised up to 4.3%, and the 10-year Treasury yield slipped to 4.84%. Spot bitcoin ETFs are also still losing cash. The U.S. funds lost $453 million on Wednesday, their seventh straight day of outflows, with BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust accounting for $329.7 million. That pushed November outflows to about $5.39 billion, extending what was already a record month for the funds. business.title: Galaxy Withdraws Call That Bitcoin’s Bear Market Ended in June
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Galaxy Withdraws Call That Bitcoin’s Bear Market Ended in June Galaxy has withdrawn its October call that bitcoin’s bear market ended in June, saying the technical signal behind it failed after seven straight weeks of losses and that the bear market is “very likely not over.” Alex Thorn, Galaxy’s head of firmwide research, laid out the reversal in a report published Wednesday and sent to clients a day earlier. “We withdraw our call that the bear market ended in June,” the report said. “The signal it rested on has failed.” The firm’s Oct. 26 note had argued that bitcoin had entered an accumulation phase. Galaxy said at the time that a weekly close back below the 50-week moving average that was not regained within a month would invalidate its technical case. That is what happened. Bitcoin closed the week ended Nov. 8 at $74,968, 0.7% below the 50-week average, after seven weekly closes above it. It then closed the week ended Nov. 15 below the 200-week average, which Galaxy has described as the floor of past bear markets. Galaxy points to $58,525 The week ended Nov. 22 closed at $61,104, 17.9% below the 50-week average and 10.4% below the 200-week average of $68,159. Bitcoin traded below its July 1 intraday low on Nov. 20 and reached $55,100 on Nov. 21, but the June 30 closing low of $58,525 held on a daily basis through Nov. 22. Galaxy now treats that level as the line to watch. A daily close below $58,525 would be “the start of a move to a materially lower low,” the report said, and the firm would not treat such a close as a buying signal by itself. History is not kind to breaks like that. In the seven prior bear market cases where bitcoin closed below a low that had stood for at least 60 days, the eventual low was at least 17% lower, with a median of 52%. Applied to the June low, that works out to about $48,500 and $28,200. Bitcoin briefly slumped below $57,500 on Wednesday morning as the Nasdaq sank, but it ended the day back above $60,000 and has not posted a daily close below $58,525. It traded near $60,800 on Thursday morning. Late by the clock, early by the depth Galaxy said two readings of the market disagree. By the calendar, this bear is old: Nov. 22 was day 412 since the Oct. 6, 2025, record, longer than the 163 to 406 days from high to low in the four prior bear markets. By depth, it looks unfinished. Bitcoin’s 53% decline compares with drops of 77% to 93% in earlier bears. It also has not closed a day below its realized price of $53,205, something every prior bear did for at least 140 days, and only two of the 13 bottom signals Galaxy tracks have been met. “The clock says this bear is overdue to end, the depth says it has further to fall, and we do not believe the price record alone can settle which,” the report said. entertainment.title: Israel Olaleye: How Can Young Nigerians Buy Land & Properties Legitimately Today?
entertainment.description: Young man with a hard hat holding a red for sale sign outside a building by Pavel Danilyuk for Pexels . My parents’ generation mostly bought land the way their parents did. Someone in the family knew someone in the village. An uncle walked the boundaries. The community remembered who owned what, and if anything went wrong, you had a face to go back to. However, my generation buys land on Instagram. I do not say that to mock anyone. I sell land for a living. When I started in real estate sales in 2023, two years after finishing a Mathematics degree at the University of Ibadan, I assumed buyers would care most about price and location. They do care. But what I hear most often is fear, dressed up as questions. Can I trust you? Is this land real? What happens if I miss a payment? After I pay, will someone come and ask me for more money? A prospective buyer once asked me, before anything else, whether community or family payments would follow after she paid for her plot. She was not asking about the land. She was asking whether the price I quoted was the real price. She had good reason to ask. Lagos State’s Property Protection Law of 2016 made it an offence to demand levies for construction on someone else’s property. Yet the same law still allows a land-owning family, with the family head’s authority, to collect a customary fee for possession, the payment many people know as a “foundation levy”. So the honest answer to her question is not a simple yes or no. It depends on the land, the family, and what has been written down. Most first-time buyers have never been told any of this. That is the gap I keep coming back to. Nobody taught us how to buy land. We learned how to save. Some of us learned how to invest in stocks, crypto or a side business. But land, the asset our parents spoke about with the most respect, has no manual. The people who used to stand in for the manual–the uncle, the community, the family lawyer everyone trusted–are often not part of how we buy anymore. So we improvise. A prospect once told me she had gone through my Instagram page carefully before she agreed to speak with me. She was checking whether I was consistent, whether my posts matched what I said on the phone, whether I had been around long enough to be real. I was flattered. Then I was worried. Because if a social media page has become part of a buyer’s due diligence, then a polished page has also become one of the easiest ways to deceive her. Instagram cannot tell you who owns a piece of land. Only a search at the land registry, done by your own lawyer, can begin to tell you that. entertainment.title: M.Inc PR Joins Industry Stakeholders to Explore Africa’s Credit Economy at ACE 2026
entertainment.description: A cross section of industry leaders and stakeholders during the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo 2026 held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. What will it take to make credit more accessible to African businesses and individuals? At the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo (ACE) 202 6, stakeholders across financial services, technology, policy, investment and entrepreneurship examined the role of reliable credit information, financial inclusion and collaboration in expanding access to capital. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. However, the expansion of digital financial services must be accompanied by responsible lending practices, consumer protection and transparency. The Expo also placed attention on young people through student-focused sessions and discussions on financial literacy. These conversations connected access to credit with the need for individuals to understand financial management, borrowing and long-term wealth creation. This focus reflects the February 2026 memorandum of understanding between CreditRegistry and the University of Lagos, through its Entrepreneurship and Skills Development Centre (ESDC), to integrate the Africa Consumer Credit Academy (ACCA) curriculum into the Centre’s programmes. The initiative is intended to strengthen financial literacy through learning opportunities, mentorship, certification and engagement with industry. entertainment.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. The Foundation is also committed to recognising academic excellence and outstanding teaching at the College. This includes recognising the College’s first-class degree graduates and NCE distinction holders, alongside the overall best NCE and degree graduates. Lecturers, selected based on student ratings, will also be honoured for their teaching contributions. The initiative builds on the Foundation’s existing investment in education, including Project Digi-Teach at Ekiti State University and GOMTECH in Are-Ekiti. For Dr. Olowolafe, the commitment to educators is also deeply personal. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). Liam Dawson provided excellent support with three wickets for 16 runs, while Sam Curran chipped in with one wicket. Jake Fraser-McGurk provided Australia with an aggressive start, scoring 22 off 11 deliveries, while Sam Harper contributed 26 off 14 balls. However, England struck at regular intervals to prevent the hosts from building any meaningful partnerships. Dawson dismissed Australian captain Mitchell Marsh for 11 before Overton took control of the innings. The pacer removed Tim David, Joel Davies, Nikhil Chaudhary, Ben Dwarshuis and other key batters to complete his five-wicket haul. Nikhil Chaudhary managed 19 runs, while Mitchell Owen scored 16, but neither could prevent Australia's collapse. Sam Curran eventually wrapped up the innings, leaving England with a target of 109 runs. sports.description: FILE PHOTO - Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta is pictured ahead of the UEFA Champions League soccer match between Arsenal and Borussia Dortmund at the Emirates Stadium. (is associated with: «Mikel Arteta demands scoring spree from goal-shy Arsenal») Adam Davy/PA Wire/dpa Mikel Arteta wants his Arsenal players to find their sense of fun by snapping out of the team’s goal-shy streak and hitting “five, six or seven”. The champions have not scored more than two goals in a Premier League match since beating promoted Coventry 3-0 on the opening day of the season and have drawn their last two fixtures. They host Manchester City at the Emirates on Sunday looking to move nine points clear of Enzo Maresca’s side, having failed to win any of their three games against City in all competitions last season. It would be a fine time for the Gunners to summon up a ruthless streak in front of goal and potentially end City’s title challenge before the end of November. “I prefer to win by five or six or seven, for sure,” said Arteta. “I’m going to enjoy the game much more, especially the last few minutes. The boys are going to have more fun. “Scoring goals, ultimately what it creates is good feeling, joy, happiness around the stands. It’s the most important thing in football.” Arsenal lead the table by six points ahead of hosting City but have scored only 17 goals in their 11 league games so far, making them just the seventh-highest scorers in the division. They are currently being outscored by eighth-placed Chelsea and have netted only two more goals than Ipswich, who are 16th. A defensive record of seven goals against has been their foundation as they seek to retain the title for the first time since 1935, and even if the goals do not flow, Arteta wants his players to relish the challenge. “The fun is being there on the grass and training,” he said. “If that’s not fun I think we have a problem. Then within that you can find moments, synergies and be a bit creative. Not to make it every single day the same. But I think the boys love to train and love to play, which is what you need.” Arteta was unable to say whether David Raya will be fit to return on Sunday having missed Tuesday’s 1-1 draw with Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League. It could mean a first league start of the season for Kepa Arrizabalaga, who came on when Raya was forced off injured against Newcastle on Saturday. It would also be a first appearance against City for Kepa since his errors led to two goals in March’s Carabao Cup final defeat. “We still have a few hours for the game,” said Arteta. “We’re just trying to get everybody back. They’re all training. “Every player has the same mindset, everyone want to be available, wants to be in the best possible condition. “The experience that Kepa has is already incredible, in the teams he’s been involved, the squads he’s been involved, the trophies that he’s won.” Last season’s meeting with City at the Emirates ended level after Gabriel Martinelli scored

The City boss also believes the Norwegian’s mood may have been influenced by a number of debatable refereeing decisions in recent games. City have won just one of their last seven fixtures in all competitions and Haaland had not scored in his last three outings for the club. The Norwegian also offered a blunt assessment of City’s performance after their midweek draw with Napoli in the Champions League, when he often cut a frustrated figure. “Erling is a winner player,” Maresca said. “It’s normal that he’s not happy when he’s not winning games but don’t forget a few weeks ago he was dancing inside the pitch. “Erling is upset just like I am upset. sports.title: "I couldn't see myself anywhere else" – El Mala loyal to Köln despite prior Dortmund links
sports.description: "I couldn't see myself anywhere else" – El Mala loyal to Köln despite prior Dortmund links Last summer, Said El Mala decided to remain at 1.FC Köln, extending his contract by one year, through 2031, which surprised the masses. "I feel the responsibility, the pressure, and the expectations that the people in Cologne have of me. But that’s a good thing for me. "Being pushed a little always helps me move forward; it usually brings out an even better performance. "Plus, I have plenty of people around me who support me through it all, so I’m quite relaxed about it," the Köln star told Kicker.de. Prior to his contract extension, El Mala was the subject of persistent interest from Borussia Dortmund at the time. BVB reportedly produced an offer of around €50million — a fee deemed not enough by Köln, and therefore the move did not materialize. But did El Mala himself even want to join Dortmund? When asked why he stayed in Cologne this summer, El Mala replied: "We were actually in talks with FC the whole time. It’s no secret that I received offers, which I did listen to. “But I couldn't see myself anywhere else,” the 20-year-old claimed, which somewhat goes against his previous media statements. At the height of the summer transfer drama, various media reports had suggested he was very keen on a move to Dortmund. Whether his comments reflect his genuine stance remains an open question. One thing is clear – a move away is off the table for now.

sports.title: 'We show class on the way out': Terry Bradshaw rips Aaron Rodgers over Steelers exit
sports.description: Terry Bradshaw spent 14 seasons with the Pittsburgh Steelers, and he wasn’t a fan of how Aaron Rodgers left the organization. The Steelers benched Rodgers on Tuesday, and less than 24 hours later, he went scorched earth on head coach Mike McCarthy during a surprise appearance on The Pat McAfee Show, prompting the team to release him and igniting one of the biggest stories in the league this year. Rodgers has already been getting a lot of criticism, with former Packers teammates James Jones and T.J. Lang both ripping the quarterback, and CBS’ Nate Burleson calling him out for dodging accountability. On Fox’s Thanksgiving pregame show, Bradshaw piled on to the criticism as he defended McCarthy and the Steelers’ organization. “They’re a classy bunch, classy organization. Mike McCarthy and I have been friends for years. Classy man. I don’t know all the details,” Bradshaw said of the Rooney family and the Steelers. Terry Bradshaw, a real Pittsburgh Steeler, spitting facts about Aaron Rodgers: https://t.co/pO2SYWWOk1 — Cory Tucek (@Cory_Tucek) November 26, 2026 Terry Bradshaw then made it clear that Aaron Rodgers’ outburst didn’t surprise him. “You know what? sports.title: Rishabh Pant record in away Tests: Is he India's best bet in SENA and overseas conditions?

List by country in table Rishabh Pant's record in away Tests is the first thing that comes up whenever India's fans and selectors discuss who can hold the batting together on a tough tour, and the numbers from the last eight years back up much of that talk. The wicketkeeper-batter is the highest-scoring designated keeper in away Test history, and his century in Wellington this month has made the debate over his place in India's overseas plans even louder. Across 36 away Tests and 63 innings, Pant has piled up 2,617 runs at an average of 43.61, with seven hundreds and 11 half-centuries to go with them. More than two-thirds of his 53 Tests have been played outside India, which makes it all the more notable that his away average sits only 1.19 below his overall career average of 44.80. In other words, the pace, bounce and swing of foreign pitches have not dragged him down in any meaningful way. England has been the busiest overseas stop for Pant, who has played 13 Tests there and scored 1,035 runs at 43.12 with four hundreds. sports.title: Calgary Flames Have a Former 50-Goal Junior Scorer Who Deserves a Bigger Opportunity
sports.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Brennan Othmann scored his first goal of the season and added an assist in the Calgary Flames’ 6-3 victory over the Pittsburgh Penguins on Wednesday. He registered five shots on goal in just 9:40 of ice time without playing a second on the power play. The 23-year-old is averaging just 9:21 through eight games this season, and it’s worth seeing what he could produce if Ryan Huska gave him more minutes alongside some of the Flames’ skilled forwards. The New York Rangers selected Othmann 16th overall in the 2021 NHL Draft. The following season, he scored 50 goals and recorded 97 points in 66 games with the Flint Firebirds of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL), adding 24 points in 19 playoff games. He won two World Junior gold medals with Canada and an OHL championship with the Peterborough Petes. His shot was one of his biggest strengths entering the draft, and he had no problem playing physically despite being one of his team’s most productive offensive players. Othmann Could Score at the Professional Level, Too Othmann scored 21 goals and recorded 49 points in 67 games with the Hartford Wolf Pack as a rookie in 2023-24, finishing second on the team in scoring and earning an American Hockey League (AHL) All-Star selection. Despite missing 10 weeks with an upper-body injury the following season, Othmann scored 12 goals in 27 AHL games and made 22 NHL appearances. That’s 33 goals in his first 94 AHL games. His production dropped last season, as he recorded 16 points in 26 games with Hartford before the Flames acquired him in exchange for Jacob Battaglia in March. He recorded seven points in 14 games with the Calgary Wranglers and three points in 19 NHL games between the two organizations. The Flames signed him to a one-year, two-way contract worth $975,000 in September. Flames Should Give Othmann Some Power-Play Time According to the AHL’s official statistics , Othmann tied Josh Doan for the rookie lead with 10 power-play goals in 2023-24 and led all rookies with 17 power-play assists. More than half of his points that season came on the man advantage, yet he’s averaging just nine seconds of power-play time per game with the Flames this season. Calgary has the NHL’s fifth-ranked power play at 25.8%, but with injuries forcing Huska to move players around , there’s room to experiment. Giving Othmann some of the minutes Ryan Strome received on the second unit Wednesday could be worth trying if Yegor Sharangovich can handle the faceoff responsibilities. The Flames have already seen what some of their younger forwards can produce with more responsibility . Othmann’s physical game makes him a useful option on the fourth line, but he’s scored at every level below the NHL. He might never become a top-six NHL forward, but playing nine minutes a night without regular power-play opportunities isn’t going to tell the Flames much about whether he can. sports.title: Renee Slegers leaves Arsenal after disappointing start to WSL season
sports.description: Renee Slegers has left her role as head coach of Arsenal following a difficult start to the Women’s Super League season for the north London club. The Gunners occupy sixth place in the WSL standings, sitting 12 points behind leaders Chelsea after 11 matches, and remain winless at home in the league this term. The Dutch manager assumed the role from Jonas Eidevall, initially on an interim basis, two years ago before guiding Arsenal to Champions League glory in May 2025. A statement on arsenal.com read: "We can confirm Renee Slegers has left her position as head coach of our women’s first team by mutual consent. "Renee departs following a disappointing start to the 2026-27 season, with assistant coach Aaron D’Antino also leaving the club. Slegers won the Champions League with Arsenal last year (Reuters) "The process of appointing a successor is under way and we will update in due course. Assistant coach Melissa Clarke-Reed will take charge of the team in the interim period. "Everyone at Arsenal would like to thank Renee and Aaron for their contributions to the club and wish them every success in their future careers." Pressure had been mounting on Slegers, particularly with Arsenal struggling to convert in front of goal, and her final match ended in a goalless draw against West Ham last Sunday. Gunners director of women’s football Clare Wheatley said: "It was an extremely difficult decision to part ways with Renee, who has led the team with dedication and commitment throughout her time here. "In leading us to glory in the Champions League and the inaugural Fifa Champions Cup, Renee has made a significant and lasting contribution to the history of Arsenal, with close support from Aaron. "After careful reflection, it is clear that results have been below the expected level and change is necessary." Arsenal have two weeks until their next fixture due to the international break, with England set to face Ukraine in a two-legged playoff as Sarina Wiegman’s side aim to secure their place at next year’s World Cup. Once the international break finishes, Arsenal will return to action without Slegers when they travel to Everton on 11 December.

De Zerbi added: “You have to analyse many things. “I think he is ready to play because he is a mature guy, he has the personality to play in every stadium, every game, but we have to analyse everything he has done this week. “The debut in the first XI, the goal, the assist, the extension of his contract. For us, for him, for the club.” De Zerbi used Dejan Kulusevski as an example for Williams-Barnett to follow and the Sweden playmaker could start one of Tottenham’s three matches over the next week after a 17-month absence with a serious knee injury. Roberto De Zerbi used Dejan Kulusevski as an example for Luca Williams-Barnett to follow (Getty) “I am thinking to start maybe not now, but I think we are very close to start a game,” De Zerbi added. “Deki is working well. I watched his games in the national team just to understand the physical condition. “He played the first game as a winger and the second game as a number 10 and especially in the second game he played very well, but we have to be good to understand the right moment to put him on the pitch. “I think medical staff, physical staff, they are working very well with him and we can’t lose any time, but we can’t take any risk because he is a special player.” While Kulusevski is close to a start, Tottenham are set to be without Savio for the rest of 2026 and beyond due to a hamstring issue sustained late on against Ipswich. De Zerbi said: “I don’t know, 50 days, 60 days, 80 days, I don’t know. When he comes back I think he will be crucial for us for the last step of the season.”

sports.title: Dan Evans to compete in controversial Gazprom-backed exhibition tournament
sports.description: Retired British tennis player Dan Evans is in the line-up for a highly controversial exhibition tournament which is sponsored by Russian energy giant Gazprom . Gazprom is majority state-owned and has been sanctioned by the UK government for its role in funding Russia’s war in Ukraine, with a 2025 statement saying its profits were “lining Putin’s war chest and facilitating the war”. The company sponsors the annual Northern Palmyra Trophies exhibition, which is held this year from 27-29 November in St Petersburg and features 12 current or former tennis players. A spokesperson for the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport told The Independent : “Our position remains that we strongly advise British athletes not to travel to Russia to participate in sports events while the illegal invasion of Ukraine continues.” Russia has not held any official ATP or WTA Tour events since the invasion of Ukraine in 2022 and Russian and Belarusian players cannot represent their country, instead competing as neutral athletes. However, exhibitions are not covered by the rules governing Tour events and players are free to play in such tournaments on Russian soil. Evans, who retired at Wimbledon this year, has not commented on his decision to take part in the event. The Northern Palmyra Trophies sees two teams face off in a mix of singles and doubles matches, with Evans drawn against world No 11, Russia’s Diana Shnaider, in a Battle of the Sexes-style clash. Frenchmen Adrian Mannarino and Corentin Moutet are also in the line-up, which primarily consists of Russian or Russian-born players. Top-100 players Anastasia Potapova , Kamilla Rakhimova, and Yulia Putintseva , who were all born in Russia, are competing, as is the retired former world No 13 Elena Vesnina . Potapova and Rakhimova have both switched nationality since the war began, with the former now representing Austria and the latter Uzbekistan. Putintseva has represented Kazakhstan since 2012. Russian 17-year-old Anna Pushkareva, compatriot Karen Khachanov , retired Serbian player Jakno Tipsarevic and Kazakhstan’s Alexander Bublik complete the line-up. Former US Open champion Daniil Medvedev competed last year but is absent for 2026. The Netherlands’ Tallon Griekspoor, who is in a relationship with Potapova, sparked a diplomatic incident when he decided to play in last year’s tournament. Dutch Foreign Minister David van Weel issued a public statement urging him to withdraw, to no avail: “It is not forbidden to participate in tournaments in Russia, but I appeal to him not to do so where possible and to look at the moral aspects.” The Russian embassy said it was “deeply concerned” by the “pressure” put on Griekspoor.
